speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Orbit geometry, multiplicities, and student research topics
summary: The actual heading and mathematical discussion occupy P001014--P001016; the wider catalogue range also includes Haefliger and Givental. Kirillov proposes topics on multiplicities, illustrates the geometry of an \(SU(3)\) orbit and its diagonal projection, and relates a recent Guillemin--Sternberg preprint to an index on a reduced space. Gelfand adds questions about duality, difference calculus and hypergeometric functions. The final remarks connect torus convexity with Newton polyhedra. The missing quotient in the multiplicity formula is mathematically consequential.

speaker: A. B. Givental
title: Relative symplectic normal forms and Lagrangian planes
summary: The manuscript heading is on P001017 and the talk ends on P001018. A relative Darboux theorem leads to local symplectic extension, the symplectic geometry of rays and obstacle problems, and the invariant alternating form on an odd symmetric power of the standard \(SL_2\)-module. An intervention attributed to Goldsheid asks for uniform approximation of a Lagrangian plane by a product of lines in fixed coordinate symplectic planes. That last question has much stronger quantifiers than the coordinatewise observation following it.

speaker: Mariusz Wodzicki
title: Local index densities and spectral boundary conditions
summary: The actual notes run from the heading on P001019 through P001021. Wodzicki reviews spectral zeta functions, local heat coefficients and the signature theorem, then explains the nonlocal boundary correction and spectral boundary conditions. Gelfand asks about additive invariants. The notebook mixes a closed-manifold formula with a boundary hypothesis and sketches a normal, rather than necessarily self-adjoint, tangential operator; these scopes are kept separate.

speaker: Mariusz Wodzicki
title: Eta regularity, spectral cuts, and local zeta invariants
summary: The actual heading is on P001022. The first part repeats the spectral boundary problem and discusses global versus local residues. Gelfand asks why self-adjointness and a filling should be needed. Wodzicki then compares zeta functions defined by two spectral cuts, relates their integer values to local residues, and writes a shifted-zeta formula with a missing power of the shift. The final p-adic analogy is not sufficiently specified to identify an automorphic theorem.
